subject: Validation of regional residency controls and tenant scrub checklist

Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Request: residency evidence + tenant wipe acceptance criteria

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As part of our diligence ahead of procurement we need a compact package that demonstrates: 1) exact regions where our dedicated tenant and backups would persist (per environment), 2) proof that snapshots and ephemeral caches are wiped on tenant deprovision, and 3) a short runbook (step-by-step) we can hand to our auditors showing how a tenant scrub is executed and validated.

Can you share a single artifact we can attach to our SOC/IT review? Ideally: a short matrix of storage locations, a scrub-playbook, and any supporting snapshots or logs. We are on a tight timeline — auditor review kicks off next week.

Regards,
Alice Reyes
Head of IT Security, FinCap Solutions
security@fincap.com

--

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Request: residency evidence + tenant wipe acceptance criteria

Marissa — adding technical notes for the evidence package. Attaching the sample snapshots tar.gz to the shared drive link; included here are the manifests and the verify script we normally run.

Operational summary (short):
- Dedicated tenant data: mounted volumes and object storage buckets are pinned to region-level only (we do not commit AZ-level guarantees).
- Backups/snapshots: periodic snapshots retained for 14 days by default for prod; retention configurable per-customer. Snapshots are stored in region-bound object storage and are included in the tenant-data-map.xlsx.
- Deprovision scrub flow (excerpt):
  1) Disable tenant routing -> drain active requests
  2) Snapshot final state with immutable manifest (stored regionally)
  3) Initiate dataset deletion pipeline (object delete + erase markers)
  4) Evict and zero KV caches on inference nodes
  5) Run verification: checksum mismatch, manifest absence check, and confirm no active mounts

Evidence we can hand back:
- Snapshot manifests (redacted) + checksums
- Operator runbook (scrub-playbook-v1.pdf) with step-by-step CLI commands and expected outputs
- A short verification script (sha256 checks) and a sample verification log (included in region-snapshots-20260512.tar.gz)

Notes/risks: we currently do not provide physical-host certificates; customers requiring host-level attestation typically contract Private on-prem or request an onsite audit.

-ben
Ben Carter
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Alice Reyes <alice.reyes@fincap.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: security@fincap.com

Subject: Re: Request: residency evidence + tenant wipe acceptance criteria

Thanks Marissa and Ben — this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups from our audit checklist:
- We do not need AZ-level info; region-level is sufficient.
- We will need: (a) a signed attestation from Redwood confirming snapshots are not replicated outside the pinned region, and (b) a short timeline for how long after deprovision a tenant is fully scrubbed (we need a conservative SLA window for the auditor).

Can you provide the attestation and a scrub completion SLA (e.g., worst-case end-to-end timeline)? If you can include approximate durations for each scrub step that will be sufficient.

Alice

Alice — attached is the final package and commitments. Key points below (this email will serve as the attestation requested):

Attestation summary (signed by Redwood Compliance):
- Redwood confirms that, for Dedicated deployments pinned to a region, snapshots and backups associated with a tenant are stored only within the specified cloud region (e.g., us-west-2) and are not intentionally replicated to other regions.
- For customers requiring additional geographic separation (physical facility details, host certificates), Redwood offers Private deployment options or an on-site audit engagement.

Scrub completion SLA (worst-case end-to-end timeline):
- Deprovision initiation to final verification completion: 72 hours worst-case for standard dedicated contracts (typical is 24–48 hours).
- Step durations (typical/worst-case):
  * Disable routing & drain: 10–60 minutes / 2 hours worst-case
  * Snapshot final state & manifest: 5–30 minutes / 1 hour worst-case
  * Data deletion pipeline (object removes + tombstone clear): 4–36 hours (dependent on dataset size)
  * KV cache eviction and node sanitization: 5–30 minutes / 2 hours worst-case
  * Verification run (checksums + manifests): 15–120 minutes / 12 hours worst-case (for very large datasets)

Evidence bundle included (links/attachments):
- tenant-data-map.xlsx (region mapping + retention windows)
- scrub-playbook-v1.pdf (operator runbook with CLI examples)
- region-snapshots-20260512.tar.gz (sample manifests + verification logs)
- Audit attestation: Redwood_Residency_Attestation_FinCap_20260515.pdf (uploaded to Drive link above)

Next steps:
- If the auditor requires a digitally-signed PDF with corporate stamp, Laura will provide the signed attestation within one business day after your confirmation that the wording is acceptable.
- If FinCap wants the scrub SLA included in contract language we can route to legal to add a clause to the DPA/Order Form.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20-min call if reviewers want a short walkthrough.

Best,
